## Q1
Which item is a problem in piggybacking acknowledgement frames?

A. There is no need to send separate acknowledgement frames.<br>
B. It requires more bandwidth.<br>
C. The data-link layer must decide how long to wait for a packet to which the acknowledgement can be attached.<br>
D. The number of acknowledgement frames decreases.

## Q1 - Options
(A) A and D only
(B) B only
(C) B and C only
(D) C only

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q20

Piggybacking reduces separate acknowledgement frames and saves bandwidth, so A and D are benefits and B is false. Its drawback is deciding how long to delay an acknowledgement while waiting for outgoing data; that is C only.

## Q2
Choose the right sequence of stages for data transmission using CSMA/CD.

A. If the channel is clear, the sender sends data.<br>
B. The sender senses the channel for activity.<br>
C. The sender waits for a random back-off time before retransmitting.<br>
D. Collision detection occurs if two devices transmit at the same time.

## Q2 - Options
(A) A, B, D, C
(B) B, A, D, C
(C) B, A, C, D
(D) C, B, A, D

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q46

CSMA/CD first senses the medium, then transmits if it is idle. A collision may be detected during transmission, after which a random back-off precedes retransmission. This is B, A, D, C.

## Q3
Assertion (A): 1-persistent CSMA provides low delay under low load conditions.<br>
Reason (R): When the channel is free, stations transmit immediately without any random delay, ensuring quick access and minimal delay.

## Q3 - Options
(A) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(C) A is correct but R is not correct
(D) A is not correct but R is correct

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q35

In 1-persistent CSMA, a station that wants to transmit senses the channel and, as soon as the channel becomes idle, transmits with probability 1, that is, immediately and without waiting any random backoff period.

Under low load, few stations are competing for the channel at any given time, so the chance that two stations sense the channel idle and transmit at the same instant is small. This lets stations gain access and finish transmitting quickly, giving low delay, so Assertion A is correct.

Reason R correctly describes this exact mechanism: transmitting immediately once the channel is sensed free, with no random delay, is precisely why access is quick under low contention. So R is both correct and the correct explanation of A.

## Q4
Arrange the following interframe time interval in increasing order.

A. PIFS (PCF Interframe Spacing)<br>
B. DIFS (DCF Interframe Spacing)<br>
C. SIFS (Short Interframe Spacing)<br>
D. EIFS (Extended Interframe Spacing)

## Q4 - Options
(A) A, B, C, D
(B) B, C, A, D
(C) D, A, B, C
(D) C, A, B, D

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q51

IEEE 802.11 defines four interframe spacing intervals that control how long a station waits before transmitting, and their durations increase in a fixed order.

SIFS (Short Interframe Space) is used for the highest-priority frames such as ACKs, so it must be the smallest gap.<br>
PIFS (PCF Interframe Space) is slightly longer and lets the point coordinator gain priority access over ordinary DCF stations.<br>
DIFS (DCF Interframe Space) is longer still and is the standard wait time for contention-based access.<br>
EIFS (Extended Interframe Space) is the longest, used after a station receives a corrupted frame it cannot interpret, giving other stations time to recover.

Mapping the labels to this order gives C (SIFS), A (PIFS), B (DIFS), D (EIFS), which is C, A, B, D.

## Q5
Which are controlled-access protocols: reservation, polling, TDMA, token passing, and CSMA/CA?

## Q5 - Options
(A) A and D only
(B) A, B, and D only
(C) C, D, and E only
(D) A, D, and E only

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q68

Controlled access coordinates stations so they take turns. Reservation, polling, and token passing are the standard controlled-access methods. TDMA is a channelization technique, while CSMA/CA is contention based.

## Q6
Identify the correct statements about multiple access techniques.

A. ALOHA is used for multiple access on a shared medium.<br>
B. TDMA uses Walsh tables for time-slot allocation.<br>
C. CSMA/CD was invented for wireless networks.<br>
D. CDMA codes are sequences generated by orthogonal codes.

## Q6 - Options
(A) A and B only
(B) B and C only
(C) C and D only
(D) A and D only

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2025 (6 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q40

ALOHA is a shared-medium multiple-access scheme and CDMA uses orthogonal spreading codes. Walsh codes are associated with CDMA, while CSMA/CD was designed for wired Ethernet, not wireless networks.

## Q7
A CSMA/CD network has bandwidth 20 Mbps. If maximum propagation time is 25 μs, what is the minimum frame size?

## Q7 - Options
(A) 500 bits
(B) 1000 bits
(C) 1500 bits
(D) 2000 bits

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2025 (6 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q75

For collision detection, a frame must last at least the round-trip propagation time: 2 × 25 μs. At 20 Mbps this is 20×10⁶ × 50×10⁻⁶ = 1000 bits. The correct option follows from the stated definition or calculation; the other options omit a necessary condition or describe a different concept.

## Q8
Consider a CSMA/CD network that transmits data at the rate of 100 Mbps over a 1 Kilometre cable with no repeater. If the minimum frame size required for this network is 1250 bytes, what is the signal speed (km/sec) in the cable.

## Q8 - Options
(A) 8000
(B) 16000
(C) 12000
(D) 20000

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q17

The minimum frame of 1250 bytes is 10,000 bits, which at 100 Mbps takes 10,000/10⁸ = 10⁻⁴ s to transmit. Collision detection requires that time to cover the round trip of 2 × 1 km. The signal speed is therefore 2 km / 10⁻⁴ s = 20,000 km/s — option D.

## Q10
Given Ethernet address 01011010 00010001 01010101 00011000 10101010 00001111 in binary, what is the address in hexadecimal notation?

## Q10 - Options
(A) 5A:88:AA:18:55:F0
(B) 5A:81:BA:81:AA:08
(C) 5A:18:5A:18:55:0F
(D) 5A:11:55:18:AA:0F

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q33

Convert each of the six 8-bit octets to hexadecimal separately.

01011010 = 5A<br>
00010001 = 11<br>
01010101 = 55<br>
00011000 = 18<br>
10101010 = AA<br>
00001111 = 0F

Joining the six pairs with colons gives 5A:11:55:18:AA:0F.

## Q11
Which of the following is correct for the destination address 4A : 30 : 10 : 21 : 10 : 1A?

## Q11 - Options
(A) unicast address
(B) multicast address
(C) broadcast address
(D) unicast and broadcast address

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q41

The least significant bit of a MAC address's first byte is the individual/group (I/G) bit, a 0 means unicast and a 1 means multicast or broadcast.

4A in binary is 0100 1010

Its last bit is 0, so this address is a unicast address, not a multicast or broadcast address.

## Q12
A host is connected to a department network which is part of a university network. The university network, in turn, is part of the Internet. The largest network, in which the Ethernet address of the host is unique, is

## Q12 - Options
(A) the university network
(B) the Internet
(C) the subnet to which the host belongs
(D) the department network

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** MAC Layer, CSMA/CD, Collision Resolution & Piggybacking
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q27

An Ethernet MAC address is a 48-bit globally unique hardware identifier administered by IEEE through Organizationally Unique Identifiers (OUIs).

- Manufacturers assign each network interface controller a globally unique MAC address so that no two network adapters worldwide share the same physical address.
- Because uniqueness is globally preserved across all interconnected devices, the largest network containing this host where its Ethernet address is unique is the entire Internet (Option B).
- Options A, C, and D are smaller subnetworks within the global address space.
